coordinates: image px of the 1920x1080 plate (= Remotion world px when the plate is drawn at 0,0 with width 1920); x right, y down; points are the CENTRE of the drawn ink line
method: Per-column darkness profile of the two ink lines (gray < ~123 counts as ink) in rows 560-860; the two darkest runs per column are the paint surface (upper) and the paint/plaster interface (lower); sub-pixel centre = darkness-weighted centroid of each run (+/-2 px); Gaussian smoothing sigma 3 px along x removes resampling jitter (max correction listed per line); resampled every 4 px from x=0 to x=1920 inclusive; normals from central differences of the resampled polyline. The drawn shape is an illustration (generated art), NOT a measured roughness profile.
verification: Plate rendered with Lanczos at 2x: the ink-line centre sits on this polyline to 0.17 px RMS / 0.6 px max (4K px), i.e. < 0.1 px at 1080p. (check image was a session scratch render, not kept) (red = surface, teal = interface, red ticks = normals every 80 px).
placement: Draw the plate (if used) at world (0,0) size 1920x1080 inside the camera Layer; the points are then world px. Recommended instead: draw the surface in code from these points (paper above, paint layer between the lines, plaster below, 4 px ink on both lines); that renders crisply at 4K and the drawn surface IS the reflecting surface.

surface.description: top of the cream paint layer (the surface light hits)

use_notes: Upward unit normal at vertex i (y down): with dx = x[i+1]-x[i-1], dy = y[i+1]-y[i-1], n = (dy, -dx)/|(dy, -dx)| (n.y < 0 = pointing up, out of the paint). vertex_normals_up holds these; for exact per-segment normals use the segment between the two vertices the ray hits.
Reflect a ray direction d off the surface: r = d - 2 (d.n) n. Intersect rays with the polyline segment by segment (it is x-monotonic, one y per x).

Spread check: a beam of parallel rays falling straight down onto the whole surface reflects within +/-59 deg of vertical (2 x max slope), RMS +/-22 deg (2 x RMS slope). One ray reflects into ONE direction; the "every which way, like a tiny lamp" picture needs a fan drawn in code at the hit point (subsurface/fine-scale scattering), labelled as illustrative.

Ink outline in the plate is ~4 px at 1080p (median dark run, slightly soft from the 1672->1920 upscale), the house outline width. If the surface is redrawn in code from these points, stroke 4 px (C.ink) on the centreline; the extracted line is the centre of the drawn stroke, so rays should reflect off the centreline (or offset by 2 px along the normal to hit the stroke edge).
